newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rail venture plans early operations - KSCI.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rail venture plans early operations - KSCI.

text.p: Mexican railroad venture Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM) plans to begin operations on May 15, instead of at the end of June as previously arranged with the government, an executive of one of TFM's partner companies said on Thursday.

TFM, a partnership between Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) and Kansas City Southern Industries (KCSI), won a 50-year concession to operate key trade route Northeast Railway from the government late last year.
KSCI President Mike Haverty told reporters TFM expected to begin operations on May 15. Government and TMM officials were not available for comment on the change in plans.

The railway's assets were expected to be handed over to TFM when the final payment on the company's stake of its hefty $1.4 billion bid was paid on June 30. The state later took a 33.5 percent stake to help reduce the company's debt load.

"The condition of the track is very good, the locomotives and the cars not so good, so we will concentrate on fixing the locomotives and cars," he said. In the first five years of operations, TFM plans to invest $900 million on the railway.

Haverty declined to discuss the company's plans with existing workers on the line, but said the company is in negotiations with the union. Analysts estimate the railway's more than 8,000 employees will need to be cut by half to meet profit expectations.
Security will be one of the line's top priorities, Haverty added. The railway has been hailed as a safer alternative than freeway transport, frequently victim to theft.
The Northeast Railway runs 6,000 miles and connects border cities with key ports and the commercial centers of Monterrey and Mexico City.
